name: Steam
description: Valve's gaming platform with a native Linux client and built-in Proton compatibility layer for Windows games.

hardwareNotes.note: NVIDIA proprietary drivers or AMD Mesa recommended for best Proton performance.

installAction.notes: Enable the multiverse repository first on Ubuntu/Debian.

name: VS Code
description: Microsoft's open-source code editor. Official .deb and .rpm packages available; also distributed as a Flatpak and Snap.

knownIssues.title: Snap version has filesystem sandbox restrictions
knownIssues.description: The Snap distribution restricts access to some filesystem paths by default.
knownIssues.workaround: Use the .deb package or Flatpak for unrestricted filesystem access.

installAction.notes: Add the Microsoft GPG key and repo first. See code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/linux.

name: Blender
description: Open-source 3D creation suite. First-class Linux support with official builds and active development on Linux.

knownIssues.title: CUDA rendering requires NVIDIA proprietary drivers
knownIssues.description: GPU rendering via CUDA is only available with the NVIDIA proprietary driver stack.
knownIssues.workaround: Use CPU rendering or switch to Cycles OptiX / HIP (AMD) for GPU rendering.

hardwareNotes.note: AMD RDNA2+ cards work well with HIP rendering. NVIDIA requires proprietary drivers for CUDA/OptiX.

installAction.notes: Official Flatpak is maintained by the Blender Foundation and typically ships the latest stable release.

name: Docker
description: Container platform for building, running, and sharing containerized applications. Native Linux support via the Docker Engine daemon.

knownIssues.title: Requires Linux kernel ≥5.15
knownIssues.description: Docker Engine relies on kernel features (cgroups v2, overlayfs) that require kernel 5.15 or later.
knownIssues.workaround: FusionOS ships kernel ≥6.1. Upgrade the kernel if running on a custom base.

knownIssues.title: rootless mode requires user namespace support
knownIssues.description: Rootless Docker requires unprivileged user namespaces enabled in the kernel.
knownIssues.workaround: Run `sudo sysctl -w kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1` or use root mode.

installAction.notes: Official install script. Review before running in production environments.

name: OBS Studio
description: Free, open-source software for video recording and live streaming. Well-maintained Linux support via V4L2, PipeWire, and Wayland.

knownIssues.title: Screen capture on Wayland requires PipeWire
knownIssues.description: On Wayland compositors, screen capture requires PipeWire and the xdg-desktop-portal-wlr or xdg-desktop-portal-gnome portal.
knownIssues.workaround: Install pipewire, wireplumber, and the appropriate portal for your desktop environment.

hardwareNotes.note: NVENC (NVIDIA) and VA-API (AMD/Intel) hardware encoding are supported on Linux.

installAction.notes: Install from the official PPA for the latest version: ppa:obsproject/obs-studio

name: Adobe Photoshop
description: Adobe's professional image editing software. No native Linux build exists. Runs via Wine with varying stability depending on version and GPU.

knownIssues.title: GPU acceleration not supported
knownIssues.description: Photoshop's GPU acceleration (OpenGL/Metal) does not work under Wine. Performance is CPU-only.
knownIssues.workaround: Disable GPU acceleration in Photoshop preferences: Edit → Preferences → Performance → uncheck Use Graphics Processor.

knownIssues.title: Font rendering inconsistencies
knownIssues.description: Some Windows system fonts are missing under Wine. Text rendering may differ from native Windows.
knownIssues.workaround: Install Windows core fonts via winetricks: `winetricks corefonts`.

knownIssues.title: Creative Cloud installer may fail
knownIssues.description: The Adobe Creative Cloud desktop app does not run reliably under Wine. Direct Photoshop installer is more reliable.
knownIssues.workaround: Use a standalone Photoshop installer (CS6 or older is most stable). Newer CC versions have lower compatibility.

hardwareNotes.note: GPU acceleration is non-functional under Wine. Expect slower performance on large files.

installAction.notes: Use Wine 8.x or later. A 64-bit Wine prefix is required for CC versions. Consider Lutris for managed Wine prefixes.

name: Microsoft Excel
description: Microsoft's spreadsheet application. No native Linux build. Runs via Wine; basic functionality works, advanced macros and add-ins have limited support.

knownIssues.title: VBA macro compatibility is partial
knownIssues.description: Complex VBA macros and Excel add-ins (VSTO, COM add-ins) do not function correctly under Wine.
knownIssues.workaround: Use LibreOffice Calc for macro-heavy workbooks, or run Excel in a VM for full macro support.

knownIssues.title: Some chart types render incorrectly
knownIssues.description: Advanced chart types may have rendering artifacts under Wine's GDI+ implementation.
knownIssues.workaround: Export charts as images, or use a VM for presentation-quality output.

installAction.notes: Microsoft 365 installer works with Wine 8.x for Excel 2016/2019. Newer M365 versions have lower success rates.

name: League of Legends
description: Riot Games' multiplayer online battle arena. Runs via Proton/Wine. Anti-cheat (Vanguard) is the primary compatibility blocker.

knownIssues.title: Vanguard anti-cheat is incompatible with Linux
knownIssues.description: Riot's Vanguard kernel-level anti-cheat requires Windows and does not run under Linux. This blocks ranked and competitive modes.
knownIssues.workaround: No current workaround. Riot has not committed to a Linux-compatible anti-cheat solution. Monitor the official Riot Linux support thread.

hardwareNotes.note: Game renders correctly under DXVK via Proton. Low-end GPUs (Intel integrated included) are generally sufficient.

gameSupport.anticheatNotes: Vanguard kernel-level anti-cheat is incompatible with Linux. Competitive play is blocked.

installAction.command: # Install via Lutris with the community LoL script
installAction.notes: Riot Client may launch, but Vanguard will block the game from starting. Not recommended until Riot provides a Linux-compatible path.

name: Cursor
description: AI-assisted code editor built on VS Code. Distributed as an AppImage for Linux. Works well out of the box on most distributions.

knownIssues.title: FUSE required for AppImage execution
knownIssues.description: AppImages require FUSE 2 to mount and execute. Some minimal distributions do not include it by default.
knownIssues.workaround: Install libfuse2: `sudo apt install libfuse2`. Alternatively, extract the AppImage: `./Cursor.AppImage --appimage-extract`.

installAction.notes: Download the latest AppImage from cursor.com. Requires libfuse2 on Ubuntu/Debian.

name: Python
description: Python runtime. Pre-installed on most Linux distributions. Multiple versions can coexist via pyenv or system package manager.

installAction.command: sudo apt install python3 python3-pip python3-venv
installAction.notes: For multiple Python versions, consider pyenv: github.com/pyenv/pyenv
